---
title: "STAT 344 Project: Average Weight of Pokemon"
output: html_document
---

## Data

We collected weights (in kg) for 100 Pokemon species. The sample was selected using stratified simple random sampling without replacement, with generation as the stratum.

```{r}
# Read the data
pokemon <- read.csv("pokemon_data.csv")

# Quick checks
head(pokemon)
length(unique(pokemon$pokemonID))
table(pokemon$generation)
summary(pokemon$weight_kg)
```

## Sample summaries

```{r}
# Population sizes and weights
generation <- c("I", "II", "III", "IV", "V",
                "VI", "VII", "VIII", "IX")

N_g <- c(151, 100, 135, 107, 156, 72, 88, 96, 120)
W_g <- N_g / sum(N_g)

# Sample mean and variance within each generation
n_g <- numeric(9)
ybar_g <- numeric(9)
s2_g <- numeric(9)

for (g in 1:9) {
  y <- pokemon$weight_kg[pokemon$generation == generation[g]]

  n_g[g] <- length(y)
  ybar_g[g] <- mean(y)
  s2_g[g] <- var(y)
}

summary_table <- data.frame(
  Generation = generation,
  N_g = N_g,
  n_g = n_g,
  W_g = round(W_g, 4),
  Mean = round(ybar_g, 2),
  Variance = round(s2_g, 2),
  SD = round(sqrt(s2_g), 2)
)

knitr::kable(summary_table)
```

## Plots

```{r, fig.width=7, fig.height=4.5}
# Histogram of weights
hist(pokemon$weight_kg,
     main = "Pokemon Weight Distribution",
     xlab = "Weight (kg)",
     ylab = "Frequency",
     col = "yellow",
     breaks = 15)
```

```{r, fig.width=7, fig.height=4.5}
# Boxplot by generation
pokemon$generation <- factor(pokemon$generation,
                             levels = generation)

boxplot(weight_kg ~ generation,
        data = pokemon,
        main = "Pokemon Weight by Generation",
        xlab = "Generation",
        ylab = "Weight (kg)",
        col = "#6495ED")
```

## Stratified estimate

The population weights are $W_g = N_g/N$. We estimate the population mean using

$$
\hat{\bar{Y}}_{st} = \sum_{g=1}^{9} W_g\bar{y}_g.
$$

Under stratified SRSWOR, the estimated sampling variance is

$$
v^2(\hat{\bar{Y}}_{st}) =
\sum_{g=1}^{9} W_g^2\left(\frac{1}{n_g}-\frac{1}{N_g}\right)s_g^2.
$$

```{r}
# Stratified mean, variance, and standard error
ybar_st <- sum(W_g * ybar_g)
v2_st <- sum(W_g^2 * (1/n_g - 1/N_g) * s2_g)
SE_st <- sqrt(v2_st)

# 95% confidence interval
lower <- ybar_st - 1.96 * SE_st
upper <- ybar_st + 1.96 * SE_st

results <- data.frame(
  Estimate = round(ybar_st, 2),
  Variance = round(v2_st, 2),
  SE = round(SE_st, 2),
  CI_Lower = round(lower, 2),
  CI_Upper = round(upper, 2)
)

knitr::kable(results)
```

The estimated mean Pokemon weight is **`r round(ybar_st, 2)` kg**, with an estimated standard error of **`r round(SE_st, 2)` kg**. The approximate 95% confidence interval is **(`r round(lower, 2)`, `r round(upper, 2)`) kg**.
